data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["The panel uses an explicit checklist, whereas source contexts often involve implicit models.","The perturbation must be designed to bypass the checklist's surface logic, which may be more constrained than perturbing an implicit model."],"overturn_conditions":["Perturbation is impossible or changes the task domain entirely.","The expert's intuition is robust to the same perturbations that fool the panel."],"shared_structure":["Both involve distinguishing causal understanding from spurious correlation in judgment.","Both require an intervention on the input to test the stability of the judgment mechanism.","Both assume that the surface form of an input can be decoupled from its deep causal structure."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_003","SRC_001"],"transfer_claims":["The error pattern on perturbed cases will differ between the panel and the expert if the checklist is merely a correlational proxy.","If the checklist captures causal structure, the panel's error rate on perturbed cases should match its error rate on unperturbed cases.","A panel merely tracking the right answer via compliance will show high variance under perturbation."]},"claim":"The non-expert panel's reliability gain is genuine only if the checklist acts as a verifiable causal proxy; evidence distinguishing this from mere compliance tracking the right answer is found by introducing adversarial feature perturbations\u2014modifying inputs to satisfy checklist items without altering the ground-truth outcome. The panel should fail on perturbed cases if it merely tracks surface features, whereas a genuine reliability gain implies the checklist captures causal structure robust to such perturbations.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The task's outcome is determined by features that are impossible to perturb independently of the outcome itself.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The perturbations required to test the causal proxy are detectable by the non-experts, triggering a suspicion heuristic.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The expert's intuition is equally susceptible to the same superficial perturbations, rendering the distinction moot.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The checklist is perfectly causally complete, meaning no feature perturbation is possible without altering the outcome.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"If the checklist is merely a correlational shortcut, non-experts will pattern-match to its syntactic form. By constructing evaluation cases where the checklist's features are superficially present but the underlying causal structure for the correct outcome is absent, one can separate causal proxy use from pattern matching. The panel's aggregate judgment should shift with the superficial features, proving mere compliance, whereas if the checklist genuinely operationalizes the causal structure, the panel's judgment should remain stable because the causal pathway to the outcome is unchanged.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
